title: Pi tool registration
responsibility: Expose the existing typed libraries to the agent as validated Pi tools and nothing more: project status and lint reads, artifact creation and mutation through the existing registries, project-type activation, stage attestation reads and writes, the research and validation capability adapters, and delegation. Own the tool schemas and result rendering; leave every business rule in `lib/`. Launch the session with Pi's built-in filesystem and shell mutation tools disabled.
notes: ⚠️ DISABLING THE BUILT-INS IS THE POINT, NOT AN OPTIMISATION. Pi's default active set includes bash, write and edit — measured, not assumed. An orchestrator holding those can write planning content around the locked, validated, atomic path that decision #88 makes the only legal one, and it will, because editing a file is easier than calling a typed tool. ⚠️ THE WIRE NAMES ARE FIXED HERE, BECAUSE A TOOL NAME IS A CONTRACT. A model is told them, a specialist allowlist names them, and the package's signature declares them - three places that must agree, so they are not improvised per wrapper. ⚠️ WHO OWNS WHICH NAMES. TSK-0044 registers exactly these 22, all `kiln_`-prefixed: kiln_create_requirement, kiln_create_assertion, kiln_create_evidence, kiln_create_runbook_step, kiln_create_question, kiln_create_decision, kiln_create_component, kiln_create_acceptance_criterion, kiln_create_task, kiln_link_evidence, kiln_unlink_evidence, kiln_revise_artifact, kiln_set_lifecycle, kiln_resolve_question, kiln_link_trace, kiln_unlink_trace, kiln_set_review_status, kiln_set_type_activation, kiln_project_status, kiln_lint, kiln_read_stage_attestations, kiln_write_stage_attestation. TSK-0045 registers six more: research_capability, research_search, research_fetch, validation_capability, validation_run and kiln_capability. TSK-0053 registers kiln_delegate beside the delegation runtime it builds. kiln_preflight remains TSK-0041's and is setup-only, removed from the effective set before the user-facing session starts, so it must never appear in the orchestrator's measured registry. ⚠️ THE FIVE SPECIALIST NAMES ARE UNPREFIXED ON PURPOSE (F79, 2026-09-12). `lib/specialists/contract.mjs` requires research_capability, research_search, research_fetch, validation_capability and validation_run BY KEY, reads their measured signatures from those keys, and `verifyChild` checks a child's registry against them. A `kiln_` prefix would break the contract and the signature check to satisfy a naming habit nobody wrote down. ⚠️ AND THE `/^kiln_/` ASSERTIONS DESCRIBE TSK-0044's 22, NOT THE PACKAGE. `test/supervisor.test.mjs` and `test/pi-session-tools.test.mjs` assert that every declared and every measured tool name starts with `kiln_`. That was true of the set that existed when they were written and is not a package-wide rule; when TSK-0045 adds its names those assertions must become EXACT-SET comparisons against the declaration rather than prefix matches, which is the stronger check in any case. ⚠️ THE ORDER THE WORK GOES IN, AND WHY. First the signature declares the names, then a check compares that declaration against what registration actually produces - by calling the registration function with a recording stub, the way the package's own test already proves it registers nothing. Without that check the declared `tools` list is the one part of the signature nothing verifies, because tools are not files on disk. Then the read wrappers, then the mutation and attestation wrappers, then the launch flags that disable Pi's built-ins, and last the real-session measurement ACC-0064 asks for - which needs a session against a loopback provider, since no CLI flag lists the active tools and exits.
